passage:
At five, Akash pulled at Mummy Ganga's dupatta ten minutes after finishing his snack. "I'm bored. Can I watch cartoons?" Mummy did not switch on the screen. She gave him a tray of wet sand from the balcony pot, a spoon and a few leaves. He sighed, then began to dig a road for a leaf-boat, and by evening his bedroom floor was full of little roads.
At nine, Akash sat on the sofa after homework with nothing planned. Without thinking, his thumb found the phone and began to scroll. Videos slid by, one after another. After half an hour, he noticed he had not laughed once and felt a bit grumpy. He remembered the leaf-boat roads. He put the phone down on the cushion, took a pencil and began drawing a map of an island. When his neighbour Uday called from the ground floor, Akash grabbed the pad and ran down, and the two of them spent the evening making the island a real one out of sand and sticks.

qa.q: What did Mummy Ganga give Akash instead of switching on cartoons?
qa.a: She gave him a tray of wet sand, a spoon and a few leaves.

qa.q: How does Akash's boredom at nine differ from his boredom at five, and what stays the same?
qa.a: At five, Akash asked for cartoons but when given sand and leaves his boredom became a game. At nine, his thumb went to the phone on its own, but he noticed he felt grumpy and chose a pencil and outdoors instead, so boredom still led to new ideas.

qa.q: What was Akash feeling after half an hour of scrolling?
qa.a: He felt flat and a bit grumpy, since the videos had not made him laugh even once.

qa.q: What could Akash's family do to help him choose an activity over the phone?
qa.a: They could keep pencils, paper and outdoor things within reach and give him unstructured time after homework without scolding him.

grounding: A child's boredom that turns to imagination with simple materials (4068) and the same child at nine choosing drawing and play over scrolling (890).
